💡 cool-retro-term | QML
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide a nostalgic and visually distinctive terminal emulator experience by replicating the appearance of old CRT monitors.
✨ Key Features: • Mimics old cathode tube screens • Eye-candy and customizable • Reasonably lightweight • Uses QML port of qtermwidget • Works on Linux and macOS
📖 Summary: Cool-retro-term is a terminal emulator that recreates the aesthetic of old cathode ray tube screens. It offers a visually appealing and customizable experience, mimicking the look and feel of vintage computer displays.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 gods-eye-view | JavaScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Providing users with a real-time, interactive, and visually rich platform for exploring live global data streams, simulating a spy satellite's perspective for situational awareness and intelligence gathering.
✨ Key Features: • Photorealistic 3D globe visualization • Live tracking of aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic, and public cameras
📖 Summary: God's Eye View is a web-based spy satellite simulator that provides live, open-source spatial intelligence on a photorealistic 3D globe. It integrates real-time data from aircraft, ships, satellites, earthquakes, traffic, and public cameras, offering a hands-free voice control interface powered by an AI agent.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 netviz | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Visually designing and animating network architectures in a browser.
✨ Key Features: • Drag and drop blocks or insert production templates • Connect blocks with edges • Build and tune custom request-flow animations • Preview animations with optional camera follow • Inspector panel to edit selected items
📖 Summary: Netviz is a browser-based application for visually designing and animating network architectures. It allows users to add components, map data flow, and create animated request paths for presentations.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 claude-swarm | TypeScript
🎯 Primary Use Case: Orchestrating parallel AI coding agents for complex, long-running autonomous development tasks with built-in safety and monitoring.
✨ Key Features: • Persistent State Management • Parallel Claude Code Workers via tmux • Git Worktree Isolation • Worker Plan Mode with Competitive Planning • Confidence Monitoring and Enforced Verification
📖 Summary: Claude Swarm is a TypeScript-based MCP server designed to orchestrate parallel Claude Code worker swarms for long-running autonomous coding sessions. It features persistent state management, Git worktree isolation, and protocol-based behavioral governance to ensure reliable and constrained AI-driven development.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 drift | Go
🎯 Primary Use Case: Enhancing the aesthetic appeal of a terminal during periods of user inactivity by displaying dynamic, artistic animations.
✨ Key Features: • 14 unique animated scenes (e.g., waveform, constellation, rain, particles, life, clock) • 9 built-in themes matched to popular terminal colorschemes • Automatic activation on idle and resumption on key press • Cross-platform compatibility (macOS, Linux, Windows) • Customizable scenes and themes
📖 Summary: Drift is a terminal screensaver written in Go that transforms idle time into ambient visual art. It offers a variety of animated scenes and themes, activating automatically when the terminal is inactive and resuming upon user input.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 ghgrab | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: To efficiently browse and download specific files or folders from remote Git repositories directly from the command line without performing a full clone.
✨ Key Features: • Browse and download files/folders from GitHub, GitLab, Codeberg, Gitea, Forgejo • TUI interface for easy navigation and selection • File preview within the TUI • Fuzzy search for quick file finding • Repo discovery and search
📖 Summary: ghgrab is a terminal-based tool for browsing and downloading files from various Git forges like GitHub, GitLab, and Gitea. It offers a user-friendly TUI for efficient file selection, previewing, and batch downloads, eliminating the need for full repository clones.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
